rationale_evidence.statement: Per-concept current-state verdicts against the Step 159 target model: Knowledge exists but semantic formalization is incomplete (KnowledgeDomain=UNKNOWN/PARTIAL); Provenance is PARTIAL (distributed traceability != first-class provenance model); deterministic assurance is CURRENT=STRONG but FULL EPISTEMIC ASSURANCE=PARTIAL; Governance is OBSERVED+DESIGNED (Architecture Board, Softwareeinfuehrungsprozess, IT Change Management, governance gates, implementation constitution, coding/naming standards already exist) with a unified machine-readable Authority->Decision->Rule->Verification model still a mapping target; Agent integration (.claude/.codex/AGENTS.md/hooks/memory/session logging) gives AgentEdge=OBSERVED but AgentEdge->GovernedKnowledgeOS needs end-to-end verification; Memory=CURRENT but Memory Governance (lifecycle to governed knowledge)=PARTIAL; Claude/Codex semantic-contract symmetry is CONCEPTUALLY ALIGNED pending implementation-conformance verification; DDD boundary status (BC_designed vs BC_implemented) is PARTIAL/UNKNOWN, requiring evidence of model ownership, independent invariants, APIs, persistence boundaries, context-specific language, and dependency relationships before a bounded context is confirmed.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Inquiry = NOT YET ESTABLISHED unless repository evidence shows otherwise. ... Determination = f(Evidence,Knowledge,Context,Method) ... DeterminationGap rather than an implementation failure. ... Authentication proves who the actor is. Whereas: Authorization determines what that actor may do. And: Governance determines whether the action should be permitted in the first place. These are distinct. ... Authorization ... UNKNOWN until we identify the actual authorization boundary.
rationale_evidence.statement: Inquiry is currently classified NOT YET ESTABLISHED (similarity of prompts/tickets/tasks/issues/investigations to Inquiry is not identity). Determination (target: f(Evidence,Knowledge,Context,Method)) may be absent as a first-class object even where PASS/FAIL/COMMENT verification results exist -- termed a DeterminationGap rather than an implementation failure. A three-way distinction is drawn: Authentication (who the actor is) != Authorization (what the actor may do) != Governance (whether the action should be permitted at all); Authorization status is currently UNKNOWN pending identification of the actual authorization boundary, formalized as target Authorization(Action,Actor,Context,Policy).

rationale_evidence.anchor: KnowledgeOS does not primarily suffer from absence of engineering mechanisms. We have many mechanisms. The larger problem is: Semantic integration between them. ... The architectural challenge is making their relationships explicit: Meaning + Identity + Lineage + Authority + Time. ... We should not start by creating ten new services. Instead: First establish semantic contracts.
rationale_evidence.statement: Major architectural discovery of Step 160: KnowledgeOS does not primarily lack engineering mechanisms (logging, memory, governance, architecture artifacts, verification, agents all already exist in some form) -- the larger problem is semantic integration between them, i.e. making explicit the relationships of Meaning+Identity+Lineage+Authority+Time. Implementation strategy consequence: do not start by building ten new services; first establish semantic contracts, then determine which existing mechanisms already satisfy them.

## Rationale
Per-concept current-state verdicts against the Step 159 target model: Knowledge exists but semantic formalization is incomplete (KnowledgeDomain=UNKNOWN/PARTIAL); Provenance is PARTIAL (distributed traceability != first-class provenance model); deterministic assurance is CURRENT=STRONG but FULL EPISTEMIC ASSURANCE=PARTIAL; Governance is OBSERVED+DESIGNED (Architecture Board, Softwareeinfuehrungsprozess, IT Change Management, governance gates, implementation constitution, coding/naming standards already exist) with a unified machine-readable Authority->Decision->Rule->Verification model still a mapping target; Agent integration (.claude/.codex/AGENTS.md/hooks/memory/session logging) gives AgentEdge=OBSERVED but AgentEdge->GovernedKnowledgeOS needs end-to-end verification; Memory=CURRENT but Memory Governance (lifecycle to governed knowledge)=PARTIAL; Claude/Codex semantic-contract symmetry is CONCEPTUALLY ALIGNED pending implementation-conformance verification; DDD boundary status (BC_designed vs BC_implemented) is PARTIAL/UNKNOWN, requiring evidence of model ownership, independent invariants, APIs, persistence boundaries, context-specific language, and dependency relationships before a bounded context is confirmed [S1352]. Inquiry is currently classified NOT YET ESTABLISHED (similarity of prompts/tickets/tasks/issues/investigations to Inquiry is not identity). Determination (target: f(Evidence,Knowledge,Context,Method)) may be absent as a first-class object even where PASS/FAIL/COMMENT verification results exist -- termed a DeterminationGap rather than an implementation failure. A three-way distinction is drawn: Authentication (who the actor is) != Authorization (what the actor may do) != Governance (whether the action should be permitted at all); Authorization status is currently UNKNOWN pending identification of the actual authorization boundary, formalized as target Authorization(Action,Actor,Context,Policy) [S1352]. Major architectural discovery of Step 160: KnowledgeOS does not primarily lack engineering mechanisms (logging, memory, governance, architecture artifacts, verification, agents all already exist in some form) -- the larger problem is semantic integration between them, i.e. making explicit the relationships of Meaning+Identity+Lineage+Authority+Time. Implementation strategy consequence: do not start by building ten new services; first establish semantic contracts, then determine which existing mechanisms already satisfy them [S1352].
